CLEAN PASS WITH A REAL CAVEAT -- the study's own codebook was OVERRIDDEN. The deposit's 'COACH_Code Book_Final_version.xlsx' labels RA_MOS_SSS_C_Q2..Q20 with the 19 MOS-SSS support items, but in RAND's subscale-GROUPED web ordering (Q2-Q9 emotional/informational, Q10-Q13 tangible, Q14-Q16 affectionate, Q17-Q20 positive social interaction), not the questionnaire's own numbering. The live data contradict that grouping and match the numbering printed in the Sherbourne & Stewart (1991) appendix (tangible = 2,5,12,15; affectionate = 6,10,20; positive social interaction = 7,11,14,18; emotional/informational = the remaining eight). Evidence, wave 1, n=2363: the shipped grouping gives a within-minus-between correlation gap of 0.1666 vs 0.0488 for the codebook grouping, against 2000 random 4-block partitions with mean 0.0004 / sd 0.0311 / max 0.1499; a 4-factor EFA yields a clean factor loading 0.70/0.72/0.81/0.77 on exactly q2/q5/q12/q15; and in all three waves the four highest-mean items are exactly q2,q5,q12,q15 (3.96/3.93/3.91/3.76 vs 2.62-3.04 for the other fifteen) -- the illness-contingent instrumental items. So the shipped item_text is the canonical questionnaire wording at each number, NOT the codebook's row-order labels. Not established by any route: the order of items WITHIN a subscale (which of q2/q5/q12/q15 is 'confined to bed' vs 'doctor' vs 'meals' vs 'chores'), which rests on the 1991 appendix numbering alone -- hence verification status PARTIAL. Language fallback: administered in Chinese; both deposited files (codebook.xlsx, raw .xlsx) contain zero CJK characters outside font names, so English base text with the _translated columns omitted. RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry would reach the same verdict; the extraction completed, gated and verified. Only new evidence about the administered Chinese wording, or the actual COACH questionnaire form, would change anything.

PASS with caveats. (1) DEVIATION FROM THE SOURCE LABELS: the deposit codebook prints item 26's anchors as 1="Always", 2="Very often", 3="Quite often", 4="Seldom", 5="Never"; the shipped option_text reverses that assignment to 1="Never" ... 5="Always" because the data contradict the codebook. Evidence (n=6,833 person-waves, study raw file): q26 correlates -0.410 with the mean of the 23 unambiguously positive QoL items -- the same sign as q3 pain (-0.542) and q4 medical dependence (-0.405) and the opposite of q1 (+0.789), q5 (+0.777), q19 (+0.812); and at baseline q26 correlates +0.187 with PHQ-9 total and +0.219 with HDRS-17 total, where q1 is -0.216/-0.202. High resp on q26 therefore means MORE negative feelings, which is the canonical un-reversed WHOQOL-BREF direction; the codebook's anchor list for that one item is simply printed backwards. q3, q4 and q26 are all stored RAW (not reverse-coded). (2) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the COACH trial was administered in Chinese to rural Chinese older adults, but neither deposited file contains any Chinese -- 0 CJK characters in the raw .xlsx sharedStrings and none in the codebook's cells. The shipped text is the study's own English codebook wording, so language=Chinese with the _translated columns omitted (the documented fallback shape). (3) WHOQOL-BREF RIGHTS not fully resolved: the wording shipped here was copied from a CC0 Harvard Dataverse deposit, and under the 2026-09-04 source-licence ruling that is what governs, so the table is not blocked. But WHO/the UK WHOQOL centre operate a user-agreement scheme for the instrument that is reportedly royalty-free only for non-commercially funded research; I could not retrieve a verbatim rights-holder sentence to that effect (who.int's WHOQOL-BREF page states no licence terms; cpcr.aut.ac.nz returned 403 and the Manchester user-information PDF failed TLS), so wording_rights=NC was NOT set -- the rule fires on a quotable clause and I have none. Worth one corpus-wide decision across the 6+ WHOQOL tables in IRW rather than a per-table guess. (4) Text transcribed literally including the codebook's own artifacts: the full-width question mark in q8, the terminal period instead of a question mark in q13, the ungrammatical "with you're the conditions" in q23, the missing spaces after commas in q26, and the inconsistent option-label casing ("very poor"/"Good"). (5) irw-validate emits one WARN, name_charset: the IRW table name 'COACH_Chen_2022_WHOQOL_BREF' is not lowercase. That is a property of the existing response table shared with the four sibling COACH tables, not of this extraction. RETRY TEST: NO -- a determinate verdict was reached, the extraction completed and passed the gate.

PASS with a disclosed caveat, not a clean-clean pass. The study administered a THAI PHQ-15 (Chinvararak, Kirdchok & Lueboonthavatchai 2021, PLOS ONE 16(8):e0255995, CC BY 4.0). The Thai ITEM STEMS are in neither the deposit nor the paper's supplements: the sole supplement (S1 File, .sav) carries only 2-4 word Thai keyword tags as SPSS variable labels ('phq ปวดท้อง', 'phq ปวดประจำเดือน', 'phq เพศสัมพันธ์'), which are demonstrably abbreviations of the items (item 11's tag is bare 'sexual intercourse' for an item reading 'Pain or problems during sexual intercourse'), and the paper's Methods never describes the PHQ-15 at all -- it only self-cites Chinvararak & Lueboonthavatchai 2016, J Psychiatr Assoc Thailand 61(4):293-306. So item_text/instructions ship the canonical ENGLISH PHQ-15 wording as the schema's translated_substitute fallback: language=Thai with item_text_translated and instructions_translated left EMPTY, which is the documented signal that the base fields are not the administered wording and the deliberate flag for a later Thai backfill. option_text is NOT a substitute -- the .sav's own value labels carry the administered Thai anchors verbatim (ไม่รบกวน / รบกวนเล็กน้อย / รบกวนมาก = 0/1/2), so those ship as administered Thai with the instrument publisher's English in option_text_translated. Two off-source attempts to recover an official Thai PHQ form from phqscreeners.com failed (the translation index is JS-driven and every guessed asset path 404s); per the standard's scoping rule that is a later pass, not a blocker. DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION, both disclosed: (1) the instructions line drops the RDC/TMD reprint's form-mechanics sentence 'Please place a check mark in the box to indicate your answer.' and corrects that reprint's typo 'how much have you have been bothered' to 'how much have you been bothered'; (2) the 'phq ' prefix on the .sav variable labels is a spreadsheet artifact and was not carried anywhere. RIGHTS: the itemtext rights rule (irw#1891) does NOT fire. The PHQ instruction manual states 'All of the measures included in Table 1 are in the public domain. No permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.', and the form transcribed carries 'Copyright Pfizer Inc. No permission required to reproduce, translate, display, or distribute.' No non-commercial clause anywhere, so no wording_rights column. This is unlike the sibling chinvararak_2021_ecr, which stayed blocked on a CC BY-NC source. RETRY TEST: NO for the shipped table -- it passed and an unchanged retry reproduces it. NO also for the Thai stems being absent from the deposit, which is determinate (the source never published them there). The one YES-flavoured residue is narrow: locating an official Thai PHQ form off-source would flip item_text from translated_substitute to administered Thai. That would take a working route into phqscreeners.com's translation library (or the 2016 Thai validation paper), neither of which is in scope here.

BLOCKED, no __items.csv written. Source is PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0279411 (CC BY; item codes Intent1-3 are verbatim the S1 Data xlsx column names, so there is no code-derivation risk). But the paper never publishes the instrument: Table 1 is titled 'Survey constructs, sample items and sources' and gives the Intent construct exactly ONE sample item, 'I will join the hospitality workforce after graduation', with no item number; Table 4 gives per-item CFA loadings by number (Item 1 .90, Item 2 .66, Item 3 .92) but no wording. There is no S2/appendix -- S1 Data is the only supporting file and its only labels are the bare column names. The cited sources (Yeung & McInerney; Yeung, Kadir, Kuppan & Foong) are school- and physics-aspiration scales that the authors adapted to hospitality, so they do not supply this study's wording. 2 of 3 items therefore have no published referent, and the 1 that does cannot be tied to a code. Shipping instrument name + the 1-6 endpoint anchors with blank item_text would be an option-only table barred by irw#1770. What IS established (see verify_choy_2022_intent_career.R): the live codes Intent1/2/3 reproduce the paper's own item numbering -- closed-form standardized loadings .910/.648/.922 vs published .90/.66/.92, scale mean 3.869 vs 3.87, SD 1.026 vs 1.02 -- though items 1 and 3 are near-tied and a 1<->3 swap is not excluded by that route. RETRY TEST: NO. An unchanged retry produces the same result; the source simply never published the wording of Intent2 and Intent3. Flipping it needs new material: the authors' bilingual questionnaire (author contact), or a later Choy/Yeung paper reprinting the full 3-item Intent scale (the 2024 Springer chapter 10.1007/978-981-97-2171-9_7 was not accessible and is the one lead worth a later look).

Clean pass with caveats. (1) item_text is a glyph rendering of the stimulus DISPLAY, not published wording: the OSF readme documents targ only as "the identifier of the specific target image" and the deposit ships no stimulus images or MATLAB task code, so each targ_NN was decoded to a (target direction, flanker direction) pair from the trial data. Two independent columns agree for all 118 participants: the correct-trial key code (98/100/102/104 = keypad 2/4/6/8 = down/left/right/up, mapping stated in the paper's Method) and the middle letter of the 3-letter feature-repetition `code` string, whose letters are pinned per participant by the congruent XXX trials. 0 disagreements, 0 targ codes resolving to two stimuli; the decode lands on a perfect 4x4 grid (targ 19-22 down flankers, 23-26 up, 27-30 right, 31-34 left). (2) instructions is blank: neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces the text shown to participants. (3) option_text holds the readme's own accuracy codes (0 = incorrect, 1 = correct) because resp in this table is trial accuracy; participants pressed one of four keypad keys, so these are not response options anyone read. (4) correct_response is the keypad key implied by the decoded target direction, derived by IRW rather than published as a key. RETRY TEST: NO -- a determinate verdict was reached and a CSV shipped; an unchanged retry would reproduce it. The only thing that would change the output is the study releasing its MATLAB stimulus files or verbatim instruction screens, which would upgrade the rendering to a transcription and could fill `instructions`. (4) AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (row-count anomaly, median 1453: targ_19, targ_25, targ_30, targ_32): these four codes are exactly the four CONGRUENT displays (all five arrows one direction) -- targ_19 down, targ_25 up, targ_30 right, targ_32 left. Every participant saw all four congruent displays, whereas the paper's random direction-pairing design gives each participant only 4 of the 12 incongruent codes, so a congruent code carries roughly 3x the trials of an incongruent one. A property of the experimental design, NOT item-code conflation and NOT an itemtext defect; no action needed.
